subject: general
question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Measles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Measles** is caused by a virus known as the **Measles virus**, which belongs to the **Paramyxoviridae family**. It is highly contagious and spreads through respiratory droplets.
 
• The symptoms of measles include **fever, cough, runny nose, inflamed eyes**, and a distinctive red rash that starts on the face and spreads to the rest of the body.
 
• Measles can lead to complications such as **pneumonia, encephalitis, and even death**, especially in children and individuals with weakened immune systems.
 
• Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent measles. The **Measles, Mumps, and Rubella (MMR) vaccine** is commonly administered to protect against measles.
 
• Efforts by the World Health Organization (WHO) and national health bodies aim to eradicate measles through vaccination campaigns worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):**

 
 
• Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, not a virus.
 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can also impact other parts of the body.
 
• It spreads through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
 
• Treatment includes a long-term course of antibiotics such as rifampin and isoniazid.
 
 
 
• **Malaria:**
 
 
• Malaria is caused by **Plasmodium parasites**, which are transmitted to humans through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• Symptoms include fever, chills, and flu-like illness.
 
• It is treated using antimalarial medications like chloroquine and artemisinin-based combination therapies (ACTs).
 
 
 
• **Cholera:**
 
 
• Cholera is caused by the bacterium **Vibrio cholerae**, not a virus.
 
• It is usually spread through contaminated food or water, leading to severe diarrhea and dehydration.
 
• Immediate treatment includes oral rehydration salts (ORS) and, in severe cases, intravenous fluids and antibiotics.
 
 
 
• **Measles – Additional Facts:**
 
 
• Measles is one of the leading causes of death among young children globally, despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine.
 
• The WHO aims to achieve a **95% vaccination rate** to establish herd immunity and prevent outbreaks.
 
• According to the WHO, over **23 million deaths** were prevented by measles vaccination between 2000 and 2018.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The measles virus is highly contagious and can remain viable for up to two hours in the air or on surfaces.
 
• Measles outbreaks are often linked to **low vaccination coverage**. Achieving herd immunity is critical to prevent the spread of the disease.
 
• In 2019, there was a significant increase in measles cases worldwide, with over **200,000 deaths** reported, mostly in children under 5 years old.
 
• Vaccination campaigns such as the **Measles & Rubella Initiative** aim to reduce measles-related mortality and achieve global eradication.
